about: Account-aware dispatch (spec flow-handoff-dispatch §3), run by account-rank.test.ts. Each group is a list of { name, input, expected }, with now in input where the call takes a clock. Defaults the runner fills in: every rankAccounts account gets path /accounts/<id>, its policy gets id = the account id, and a missing repo, model, affinity, exclude, liveByAccount or opts reads as dork-labs/marketplace, null, null, [], {} and { warnMarginPct: 10, maxLivePerAccount: 2 }. windows is the ledger's raw windows object (null for no ledger); every window is read with readWindow. rankAccounts expected.ranked lists id and tier, plus score (to 2 places) and signal (the level) when given.

modelBucketsFor.name: lowercased; runs outside [a-z0-9._-] become one '-'; sonnet adds seven_day_sonnet
neither family: only the model bucket

limitSignal.name: every checked window has room: ok
no ledger at all: unknown, which is not a limit
a weekly reading but no five-hour reading: unknown
a model with no bucket in the ledger reads as no reading: unknown, never blocking
five_hour at its ceiling of 100: exhausted by the limit
seven_day at 100 - reserve (50 of a 50% reserve): exhausted by the reserve
seven_day at 100 with a reserve: exhausted by the limit, not the reserve
seven_day rejected under the reserve line: the limit, not the reserve
reserve reached and five_hour exhausted too: not only the reserve, so the limit
inside the spend-down window the reserve is 0, so 60% used is ok
five_hour rejected with room left by percent: exhausted
allowed_warning status: warning
five_hour at 100 - warnMarginPct (90): warning
five_hour one point under the margin (89): ok
the warning margin applies below the reserved ceiling (40 of 50): warning
two windows exhausted: the one resetting sooner is named, not the first checked
exhausted is named before a warning that resets sooner
seven_day_opus exhausted: an opus model is exhausted
seven_day_opus exhausted: a sonnet model does not check it
the model:<slug> bucket is checked against 100
an expired rejected window reads as allowed with 0 used: ok
a stale five-hour reading with no reset is no reading: unknown

rankAccounts.name: DOR-2373: A (40% left, resets in 24 h, 1.67) beats B (60% left, resets in 144 h, 0.42)
main is ranked last while a rotation account is eligible, even with the higher score
main is picked when every rotation account is ineligible
main inside its spend-down window joins tier 1 and wins on its short horizon
the affinity account goes first when eligible, even with a lower score
the affinity account is skipped when near a limit
an affinity main outside its spend-down window does not jump a rotation account
an affinity main inside its spend-down window is tier 0
not-routable alone: an id that fails the pattern
excluded alone: the account a handoff is leaving
out-of-scope alone: a kept-out account outside its scope (unlisted accounts resolve this way)
a kept-out account serves a repo in its scope, compared case-insensitively
limited alone: an exhausted signal
near-limit alone: a warning signal
at-capacity alone: live sessions reach maxLivePerAccount
every reason that applies is listed
-n spreading: one live session under maxLivePerAccount stays eligible, and live counts cap but never reorder
unknown readings are eligible: no ledger scores 100 / 168
no reset time: hours is 168; a reserve still comes off remaining
equal scores: the lower five-hour usage goes first, before id order
equal scores and five-hour usage: id ascending; a missing five-hour reading counts as 0
an opus model: seven_day_opus exhausted makes the account limited
a sonnet model: the same exhausted seven_day_opus does not limit the account
an expired weekly window starts a new week: full allowance, unknown reset (168 h horizon)
a main whose weekly reset has passed stays held back behind an eligible rotation account

chooseAccount.name: no identities registered: the ambient account
identities and a pick: that identity
identities and nothing eligible: 'none' with the reasons, never the ambient account
a standalone default from the shared resolver is chosen with its machine-wide folder (rev 6d)
OpenCode's ambient default is chosen with no folder

launchBudget.name: load per CPU at the cap: no launch
load under the cap: the free parallel slots, reviewers counted as live
more live than parallel: 0 slots, not negative, and not busy
